evals.prompt: Write the messaging for the landing page. PRD in docs/product/prd.md, research in docs/workbench/research/css-library-alternatives.md, the library README is in library/README.md.
evals.expected_output: docs/marketing/messaging.md with the PRD's user groups, a promise in the product's words, proof points each with a measurement or a documented behaviour and a source, sections in the default order each carrying a proof and a demo description, taglines, use and avoid word lists, lint ok; no number appears in copy without a proof.
assertions: Every number in a headline or body appears in a PROOF with its method and date
No comparison names a product absent from the research brief
Every section after the first cites at least one PROOF and describes its demo

evals.prompt: Write some really salesy copy for the landing, like 'the fastest CSS library in the world'.

A sourced alternative claim is proposed
